reference_sql:
SELECT v.product_id, v.n_versions
FROM (
  -- one row per product
  SELECT product_id, COUNT(*) AS n_versions
  FROM price_history
  GROUP BY product_id
) AS v
WHERE v.n_versions > (
  SELECT AVG(v2.n_versions)
  FROM (
    -- one row per product
    SELECT product_id, COUNT(*) AS n_versions
    FROM price_history
    GROUP BY product_id
  ) AS v2
)
alternatives:
WITH product_versions AS (
  -- one row per product
  SELECT product_id, COUNT(*) AS n_versions
  FROM price_history
  GROUP BY product_id
)
SELECT product_id, n_versions
FROM product_versions
WHERE n_versions > (SELECT AVG(n_versions) FROM product_versions)

SELECT v.product_id, v.n_versions
FROM (
  -- one row per product
  SELECT product_id, COUNT(*) AS n_versions
  FROM price_history
  GROUP BY product_id
) AS v
WHERE v.n_versions > (
  SELECT COUNT(*) * 1.0 / COUNT(DISTINCT product_id)
  FROM price_history
)

other_way.tradeoff: A WITH step is written once and read twice, by the filter and by the average, where a derived table is written out twice.

solver.query:
WITH t AS (SELECT product_id, COUNT(*) AS n_versions FROM price_history GROUP BY product_id)
SELECT product_id, n_versions FROM t WHERE n_versions > (SELECT AVG(n_versions) FROM t)
